newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Vishay says to continue Israel expansion.
newsitem.headline: Vishay says to continue Israel expansion.

text.p: Pennsylvania-based Vishay Intertechnology said on Thursday it will continue to expand in Israel despite the government's intention to cut investment subsidies.

"The Israeli government's proposed reduction of investment grants from 34 percent to 20 percent does not affect Vishay. All of Vishay's approvals for expansion in (its plants in) Dimona, Beersheba and Migdal Ha'Emek with government grants of 38 percent or 34 percent will not be affected by such a decision if implemented. Vishay's expansion in Israel will continue as planned," the company said in a statement.

The company said it may, however, cancel plans to set up two new plants in Israel, a $50 million plant in Ofakim and a $150 million plant in Beersheba, if its request for a grant is not approved soon.
Under the government's proposal, which still needs parliamentary approval, grants in top priority development areas would be cut from 34 percent to 20 percent in 1997.
The Investment Centre, the Industry and Trade Ministry's arm that approves investment subsidies, has delayed approving new projects because it has run out of money.
The Treasury will probably increase the Investment Centre's 1996 budget by 300 million shekels to allow it to continue approving projects this year, a Treasury spokesman said.
Vishay, with annual sales of $1.2 billion, is the largest producer of passive electronic components in Europe and the United States.
